subject: Mathematics

standards.statement: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities.

know: Definition of a ratio as a comparison of two quantities
Three different ways to write a ratio (3:1, 3 to 1, 3/1)
do: Identify ratios in real-world contexts (classroom, school, home)
Express the same ratio in three different notations
Describe a ratio relationship using proper vocabulary
Create simple ratios from given quantities
demonstrate: Given a context, write a ratio in at least two forms
Explain what a ratio tells you about a situation
Identify when two descriptions refer to the same ratio

prerequisites: Multiplication and division facts (fluency helpful, not required)
Understanding of whole numbers and basic comparison concepts
common_misconceptions: Students confuse ratios with fractions (3:1 is not 3/1 as a fraction)
Students don't understand that order matters (think 3:1 = 1:3)
Students treat ratios as requiring simplification like fractions
Students confuse ratio with just counting one quantity

centric_alignment.proficiency_basic: I can explain the concept of a ratio and identify ratios in real-world situations
centric_alignment.proficiency_intermediate: I can express ratios in multiple forms and explain how ratios describe relationships
centric_alignment.proficiency_advanced: I can analyze and create ratios in complex situations and justify my reasoning

standards.statement: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0, and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship.

know: Definition of a unit rate (quantity per 1 unit of another quantity)
How to find a unit rate by dividing the first quantity by the second
Notation and language for unit rates (miles per hour, cost per item, etc.)
That equivalent ratios produce the same unit rate
do: Calculate unit rates from given ratios
Identify unit rates in real-world contexts (speed, price, density)
Use rate language to describe relationships
Determine which unit rate is better (e.g., lower price per item)
demonstrate: Given a ratio, calculate the unit rate and explain what it means
Compare unit rates to make decisions (which is a better deal)
Convert between different unit rates (mph vs. meters per second)

prerequisites: Division skills and understanding of division as sharing
Decimal fluency helpful for real-world rates
common_misconceptions: Students calculate unit rate incorrectly by reversing the division
Students don't understand that different unit rates for same ratio are equivalent
Students forget the 'per' language when describing unit rates
Students can't connect unit rate back to the original ratio

centric_alignment.proficiency_basic: I can calculate a unit rate and explain what it means in a given context
centric_alignment.proficiency_intermediate: I can identify and calculate unit rates in various contexts and use them to make comparisons
centric_alignment.proficiency_advanced: I can analyze complex rate situations, convert between different units, and justify decisions based on unit rate comparisons

standards.statement: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems, e.g., by reasoning about tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number lines, or equations.

know: Multiple strategies for solving ratio problems (tables, tape diagrams, number lines, equations)
When each strategy is most useful
How to set up and solve multi-step ratio problems
That equivalent ratios can be found by multiplying or dividing both parts
do: Solve one-step ratio problems using multiple strategies
Solve multi-step ratio problems with real-world context
Create and use tables of equivalent ratios
Use tape diagrams or number lines to solve problems
Write and solve simple equations based on ratios
demonstrate: Select appropriate strategy for given problem
Solve problems and justify solution method
Explain why a solution makes sense in context
Create word problems for given ratio solutions

common_misconceptions: Students add instead of multiply when finding equivalent ratios
Students don't check if their answer makes sense in the context
Students use wrong operation or strategy for problem type
Students confuse which quantity corresponds to which in tables or diagrams

centric_alignment.proficiency_basic: I can solve simple ratio problems using one strategy and explain my work
centric_alignment.proficiency_intermediate: I can solve multi-step ratio problems using multiple strategies and explain why my solution makes sense
centric_alignment.proficiency_advanced: I can solve complex ratio problems, select the most efficient strategy, and justify my reasoning with multiple representations

unit_arc.description: Students develop conceptual understanding of what a ratio is and learn to represent ratios in multiple ways
Students apply ratio understanding to calculate and compare unit rates in real-world contexts
Students use multiple strategies to solve multi-step ratio and rate problems

summative: Unit test with multiple choice and short answer

for_advanced_learners: Explore ratios with irrational numbers or decimals
